newsitem.title: USA: Chevron says expects Kazakh pipeline deal in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chevron says expects Kazakh pipeline deal in 1996.

text.p: Chevron Corp's chairman said Monday he expected an agreement to build a pipeline in Kazakhstan by the end of this year, noting parties are "very close" on securing a deal.
Chevron Chairman and CEO Ken Derr, speaking to reporters at the American Petroleum Institute's annual meeting, said a final agreement awaits a tax ruling by the Russian government.
Chevron produces oil in Kazakhstan at its Tengiz field.
Derr said current Tengiz production is more than 130,000 barrels per day, adding that he hoped that figure would rise to 150,000 bpd in 1997.
"We are currently debottlenecking facilities and we'll have to see how that goes to get a better idea on where production will be in 1997," Derr said.
Chevron hopes to have the pipeline built in two years, which would allow production to increase to more than 250,000 bpd by providing an export channel.
Derr noted Chevron's plans for 1997 call for a $5.5 billion capital expenditure program focusing on international exploration and production and deepwater Gulf of Mexico investment.
